Body: I agree. Hitting "undo previous message" fully stops whatever process was going, even though you're only stopping the queued message. Then you have to tell the model to "proceed" or whatever to get it to pick up where it left off (if it can).

@powoct Good news — with a correct local setup, **the fix works in my environment**, in both normal and private windows, including the cold-start first input. Details and the traces you asked for below. One important correction about my earlier testing first.

## A correction about my first reproduction

My original report (and my earlier comment) was against a setup I believed was "this branch, dev mode". It turns out my local `opencode serve` was serving the **production `https://app.opencode.ai` bundle**, not my checkout — when the embedded web UI (`opencode-web-ui.gen.ts`) is absent, the server falls back to proxying the upstream app. I confirmed this by matching the served bundle hash byte-for-byte with `app.opencode.ai` (`index-Ca69RsoK.js`). So the per-letter splitting I reported was the **unpatched production** behavior, and said nothing about your branch either way. Apologies for the noise.

## Correct test against this branch (production build)

I then built the branch locally and served the real patched bundle via `vite preview` (bundle `index-Co4JMD1P.js`), with the API proxied to a backend running this checkout (`3c820da16`). I tested in **both a normal window and a private window**, three rounds each, with the macOS built-in Simplified Chinese Pinyin IME:

- **Round 1 — cold start, first prompt input in a fresh session: WORKS.** Single continuous composition `n → ni → ni h → ni ha → ni hao`, candidate window appears, Space commits 你好. No per-letter split.
- **Round 2 — after sending one message: WORKS.** Same continuous composition, Space commits 你好.
- **Round 3 — after two messages: WORKS.** Same. Plain ASCII insert/delete afterwards also normal.

The per-letter split I saw before is **gone with the patched build** — including the first-input cold-start case, and in both window types.

## Answers to your five questions

1. **Versions**: Safari 26.6 (21624.4.5.11.5), macOS 26.6 (25G72). My original (broken) repro was in a private window. The patched build works in **both** normal and private windows.
2. **Build mode**: The splitting I originally saw was effectively **production** (the proxied `app.opencode.ai` bundle), not vite dev. The **patched production build** does not reproduce it in either window type.
3. **Event trace** (patched production build, cold-start first input, typing `nihao` then Space):

```
1611ms compositionstart
1612ms compositionupdate   data:"n"
1612ms beforeinput  insertCompositionText  isComposing:true  data:"n"
1615ms DOM-MUTATION x2  childList,characterData  textContent="n"
1616ms input        insertCompositionText  isComposing:true  data:"n"
1655ms keydown      keyCode:229  isComposing:true  key:"n"
1674ms keyup        keyCode:78   isComposing:true  key:"n"
1763ms compositionupdate   data:"ni"        <- same composition continues, NO compositionend
1927ms compositionupdate   data:"ni h"
2027ms compositionupdate   data:"ni ha"
2087ms compositionupdate   data:"ni hao"
2141ms keyup        keyCode:79   isComposing:true  key:"o"
2252ms beforeinput  deleteCompositionText
2254ms beforeinput  insertFromComposition  data:"你好"
2271ms DOM-MUTATION x3  textContent="你好"
2271ms input        insertFromComposition  data:"你好"
2271ms compositionend  data:"你好"
2276ms keydown      keyCode:229  isComposing:false  key:" "   <- Space picked the candidate
3051ms keydown      keyCode:13   Enter  -> message submitted with 你好
```

   The key difference vs. my broken trace: with the patched build the composition **stays open across all five letters** (no `compositionend` until the candidate is committed), whereas the unpatched build fired `compositionend` after every single `keyup`.
4. **Control test**: bare `contenteditable`, the Safari address bar, and Spotlight all compose 你好 normally — my IME stack is healthy.
5. **Input settings**: input sources are just the macOS built-ins — Simplified Chinese Pinyin (`com.apple.inputmethod.SCIM.ITABC`, enabled + selected) plus

Updated with `v2` and resolved both conflicts, preserving the isolated Markdown sanitizer and the Mermaid regression coverage.

Drive handling is not hardcoded: runtime matching accepts any ASCII drive letter, case-insensitively. Added explicit `D:/`, `Z:\`, and `file:///d:/` cases alongside POSIX and relative paths.

Security review found and fixed one browser-origin issue: opening a raw SVG blob as a document retained the app origin. SVGs now use opaque-origin data URLs, consistent with the existing media viewer. The browser regression test reproduced the inherited origin before the fix and verifies `location.origin === "null"` afterward. Inline SVG images still cannot run scripts or load external resources.

No new server-to-local shell or Node execution path was found in this PR. Image reads go through the selected server's authenticated file API; they do not add local filesystem, shell, or desktop IPC calls. Desktop renderer settings remain `nodeIntegration: false`, `contextIsolation: true`, and `sandbox: true`. Remote image requests receive no API authorization header, and forged loader metadata is removed. This is a focused source and Chromium review, not a full application audit or a guarantee against browser decoder vulnerabilities.

Validation: 67 focused unit cases, all 11 Markdown browser tests, app/session-ui typechecks, formatting, and diff checks pass.

@anyingiit Thank you for the thorough follow-up — tracking down the serve fallback and re-testing with the real build is exactly what was needed, and the traces are perfect. Much appreciated.

Summary for reviewers:

- The earlier "doesn't fix it" report is **retracted**: the local `opencode serve` was silently proxying the **unpatched production `app.opencode.ai` bundle** (the fallback when the embedded web UI is absent), confirmed by bundle hash. So the per-letter splitting shown there is what production ships today — it is the bug this PR fixes, not a counter-example to it.
- With the actual patched build, the fix is now **verified on two independent environments**: macOS 26.6 (25G72) / Safari 26.6 (@anyingiit — normal + private windows, including cold-start first input), and macOS/Safari 26.5.2 → 26.6.2 (mine — production deployment, with event traces captured before and after the OS update, identical ordering).
- The traces pin the defect signature precisely: **unpatched, Safari fires `compositionend` after every `keyup`**, splitting the composition into per-letter commits so the romaji leaks as plain text and the confirming key degrades to a plain Enter; **patched, the composition stays open across all keystrokes** and the confirming key arrives as `keyCode 229` within the `compositionend` guard window, so it is correctly ignored.

# Comentario para el issue #40399

Still reproduces on **1.18.23** (Windows 11 Pro, `opencode web`, Chrome desktop and Android).

**Root cause** — the server is fine; it's the web client. The server normalizes the path and
returns sessions correctly for any casing:

```
GET /session?directory=c%3A%5Cprojects%5Cdemo&roots=true  →  sessions (stored as C:\Projects\demo)
```

But the client compares paths case-sensitively:

1. The per-project path store is only set when
   `global.path.directory === directory` — exact string match against the path typed when
   connecting the project (`"c:\projects\demo" === "C:\Projects\demo"` → false, so `path` is never set).
2. The session list filter is
   `normalize(session.directory) === normalize(path.directory)`, where `normalize()` replaces
   `\` with `/` and trims trailing slashes but does **not** fold case.

With a lowercase drive letter, (1) fails, `path.directory` stays `undefined`, and the list
filter matches nothing → "No sessions yet", while creating sessions/chatting still works
(the server normalizes on create).

**Workaround:** disconnect the project and reconnect it with the exact canonical casing
(`C:\Projects\demo`), or open `http://<host>:<port>/<base64 of canonical path>` directly.

**Suggested fix:** fold case in the path normalizer on Windows (or always compare against the
server-normalized path from `GET /path` instead of the raw user input).

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #44581: Same root cause — SSE reasoning stream deltas stored as one object per chunk instead of being folded, causing context explosion and token inflation across turns.

**Post-review correction (from a critical review):** this issue has been updated to fix several inaccuracies in the original report: (1) the duplicate reasoning objects are created *throughout* the stream (all carrying the identical final text), not appended after stream completion; (2) the chars-per-token ratio is ~3.65–3.71, not ~3.3; (3) the 'model loses its own reasoning' claim was retracted — the live test showed the visible assistant answer was retained (model quoted exact figures) while only the oversized reasoning metadata was excluded; (4) 'provider-billed' tightened to provider-reported usage; (5) this duplicates #44581. Verified numbers and full corrections in the updated body.

Confirmed independently with detailed evidence — see #45791 (same root cause). Key findings: a live reproduction on v0.0.0-beta-18414 stored **792 identical full-text reasoning objects (32,251 chars each = 25.5 MB) for a single turn**; per-request provider-reported input in a real session grew 14,972 → 156,718 → 171,779 → 300,968 tokens (555k input + 640k cache-read total for a 12-record session, /bin/zsh.054, only 2,134 output tokens). The duplication lives in `state.reasoningDetails[0].text` (top-level `text` is empty on all but the first object), and the objects are created throughout the stream sharing one finalized metadata blob. Suggested fix (in #45791): coalesce reasoning events into one logical part, attach final metadata once without shared references, and defensively deduplicate outgoing `reasoning_details` for existing corrupted sessions.

@junwha 
> Use a litellm proxy

Does it generate fake / empty streaming tokens in response? Opencode has some kind of built-in timeout (around 300 seconds, I think). If it doesn't receive at least one streaming response token within that limit, it will consider API endpoint timed out and retry the request. And I often encounter situations when it takes more than 300 seconds to generate the full non-streaming response.
Here is what Google AI told me but I'm not sure if it's true:

> While LiteLLM does have an internal "fake streaming" mechanism (MockResponsesAPIStreamingIterator) that translates a stream=true request into a non-streaming upstream call, it waits for the complete upstream non-streaming response to finish before it splits that response up into chunks and sends them back to your consumer. It does not proactively emit periodic "keep-alive" or empty filler tokens to the client while the upstream endpoint is still thinking.
>
> To prevent opencode from timing out while waiting for a slow non-streaming backend, you will need to intercept the request and handle the keeping-alive yourself.
> 
> Sources :
> - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/30208
> - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/21090
> - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/5416

- No recognized issue template was used (Bug Report, Feature Request, or Question). Please use one of the three templates.
- The report reads as AI-generated: it describes vague "community users" and "community feedback" without any first-hand reproduction steps, actual error messages, or personal environment details.
- A Bug Report requires a real description with steps to reproduce, expected behavior, actual behavior, and your own environment info — not a summary of other issues.
- The content appears to be a restatement of existing issues #45791 and #45788 rather than a new, independently reproducible report.

Please edit this issue to address the above within **2 hours**, or it will be automatically closed.

- #45791: Session reasoning parts duplicated per streamed chunk inflate context to 300k+ tokens and explode session storage (same root cause as described here)
- #45788: opencode serve from source silently serves the production web UI instead of local code (same session handling issue referenced here)

If you believe this was flagged incorrectly, please let a maintainer know.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #24316: Progress halts with naked tool call in the console — describes the same symptom of raw XML tool-call tags (including `<parameter>` fragments) leaking into the TUI display instead of being parsed. Also references PR #27984 which proposes stripping dangling XML artifacts from streaming text deltas before they reach the TUI.

Resolved the v2 lockfile conflict in faeca49633, retaining the Vite tooling upgrade and the deduplicated Kobalte/Solid primitives. All eight current PR checks passed, including Linux/Windows unit tests, Linux/Windows production E2E and service-worker tests, and typecheck: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/33131432449. Local verification also passed the frozen lockfile install with Bun 1.3.14 and the targeted production UI regressions.

Adding a +1 / confirmation for this — same symptom on a recent release.

**Environment:**
- opencode binary `1.18.23` (latest), `opencode-ai@1.18.23`
- node `v24.18.0`
- Linux (Termux/Android, arm64), default setup, no plugin

**Symptom:** Intermittently, raw tool-call tags (`<parameter name="...">...</parameter>`, stray `<parameter>`, `</parameter>`) appear as literal text in the TUI above the assistant message. Tools still execute fine — it's a rendering/parsing artifact. Most likely to happen on multi-step turns (bash + edit/glob back-to-back).

**Re: PR #27984:** Confirming what @Gr33n93 reported on 1.18.10 — the proposed fix is still open and **not** present in 1.18.23, so this is still reproducible on the latest release.

Happy to add a screenshot on next occurrence. Thanks for tracking this — would love to see #27984 (or the #30633 approach) merged.

Closing this as a duplicate — before opening it I hadn't seen #24316, but the bot's suggestion is correct: same raw-XML-tool-call-leaks-into-TUI behavior, and it still reproduces on 1.18.23 (PR #27984 / #30633 not yet merged into a release).

Related API request: #45801 asks for server-side transcript search results to carry the revision defined here. Without that composition, a bounded client cannot tell whether paginated matches still belong to the transcript version it searched.

Related API request: #45801 asks for each transcript-search result to expose a directly navigable target. That target should compose with the rank/seek contract proposed here so clients can open a match without walking every preceding cursor.

Additional V1-to-V2 migration context from CodeNomad:

V1 did not expose a transcript revision either, but `session.messages` returned the complete projected transcript in one response. CodeNomad therefore did not combine independently fetched message pages, and could reconcile that one response against events received during hydration with a local store counter.

V2 introduces a different consistency problem because the transcript is now consumed through multiple opaque cursor requests. CodeNomad keeps a bounded 200-message resident window and may traverse further pages for search. If compaction, revert, append, or an in-place content update occurs between requests, the client cannot determine whether the collected pages describe one server snapshot. CodeNomad's local revision counter only records events that this client observed; it cannot establish the revision used by the server for each page or recover authority after reconnect.

This is therefore not a missing V1 field requested for parity. It is snapshot authority required by V2 pagination. A revision on each message-list/search response would let bounded clients discard mixed reads and restart from one known transcript state.

Hello,

I wanted to tell you this idea because I honestly don't know who else to tell.

I came up with something that I think could potentially accelerate the inference of medium-sized AI models dramatically using RAM alone.

Please, I'm not joking, and I don't think this is a silly idea. Give me two minutes and let me explain.

Imagine having a 27B model such as Qwen 3.8 27B that takes around 30 GB of storage.

For users who don't have two 16 GB GPUs or a 32 GB GPU, but who do have 128 GB of RAM — or even 64 GB or more — I was thinking about the following:

What if we loaded the same model into RAM two or four times?

In other words, we would replicate the model weights multiple times in RAM when extra memory is available, and distribute those copies across the memory channels of the system.

For example, a system with 64 GB of RAM might have two memory channels, while a 128 GB system could have four channels.

Then, the CPU's multithreaded cores could access specific layers that are read very frequently — for example, particular experts in a Mixture-of-Experts model or other frequently accessed layers — in parallel.

This would not simply be traditional memory interleaving.

The idea would be to create parallelism at the information level by duplicating the most frequently needed parts of the model in RAM, so that multiple memory channels could serve those reads simultaneously.

For example, with 128 GB of RAM, you could potentially have four copies of a ~30 GB model in memory and use different CPU threads to access the important layers in parallel.

The idea is that, because the model is replicated across the RAM channels, the system could potentially read the most important parts of the model much faster.

For example, in a server with 8 DIMM slots, you might have four memory channels with two DIMMs per channel.

I think this could potentially multiply inference performance significantly for medium-sized models running primarily from RAM.

Obviously, it would only make sense for medium-sized models and systems with a large amount of RAM. But if it worked, you could potentially get much higher inference performance without needing expensive GPUs.

I'm not claiming that this definitely works — I'm asking you to take a look at the concept and see whether there is something technically interesting here.

WITH THIS METHOD, INFERENCE COMPUTATION WOULD NOT HAVE THE CPU, GPU, AND RAM FIGHTING WITH EACH OTHER THROUGH MEMORY INTERLEAVING, BECAUSE EVERY CORE THREAD COULD ACCESS THE HOTTER EXPERT LAYERS WHERE THE INFORMATION IS CONTAINED, WITH A MIRROR OF THE WEIGHTS IN EVERY RAM CHANNEL.
